title: Encoding Is Not Understanding
hook: Saving a note is not the same as being able to use it under load.
excerpt: A thin definition page: encoding stores the packet; understanding is retrieval that still works when you are tired.
lede: Archives grow. Fluency does not, unless you practice retrieval.
author: Nitish Chauhan

sections.heading: Encoding
sections.body: You captured the words. The file exists. That is necessary and nowhere near sufficient.

sections.heading: Understanding
sections.body: You can restate the lever, apply it to a new case, and teach it without opening the note.

data.title: Smell test
data.body: If you need the original chat to explain the idea, you encoded it. You have not metabolized it.

takeaway: Measure understanding by use under load, not by folder size.
caveat: Definition sketch for systems design, not educational psychology coursework.
